result.summary: Updates the Guix build scripts for Linux and Windows to map the entire DISTSRC root instead of DISTSRC/src in -fdebug-prefix-map. This ensures generated sources located in the build tree receive relative paths in debug symbols rather than keeping absolute build directory paths.
result.problem: Debug symbols produced by Guix builds use relative paths for source files under src/, but generated source files (such as capnp IPC proxies) residing in the build tree retain absolute paths from the Guix build container. Having both relative and absolute paths complicates source path mapping in debuggers.
evidence: Description: 'Generated sources (for example the capnp proxies) are in the build tree, outside ${DISTSRC}/src, so their debug info kept the absolute /distsrc-base/distsrc-<commit>-<host>/build/... path... With two kinds of paths, it is hard to set up source path mapping in a debugger.'
result.scope_notes: Touches 4 Guix build shell scripts (build_linux.sh, build_linux_gui.sh, build_win.sh, build_win_gui.sh) modifying one compiler flag in each.
result.card: Updates Guix build scripts for Linux and Windows targets to apply -fdebug-prefix-map to the repository root DISTSRC rather than DISTSRC/src. Previously, generated files like capnp proxies retained absolute build-container paths in debug symbols while normal sources were relative, making debugger source resolution difficult. All source paths in Guix debug symbols are now uniformly relative to the repository root. This addresses issue #34414.

risk.why: A mistake in Guix build compiler flags could break build reproducibility or corrupt debug symbol outputs for Linux and Windows releases.
